text:
maya: Hey team, seeing a sharp latency spike and a KC/prefix cache hit-rate collapse in hosted-nyc-pool-3 since ~12:21 UTC. p50/p99 both up ~3-4x, throughput down ~30%. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

alex: Which model/route? Any recent deploys or config changes?

maya: Route: /v1/generate (r-instruct-13b). No application deploys in the last hour AFAIK. Attaching quick metrics snapshot:

```
kv_cache.hit_rate: 92% -> 11.8%
evictions_per_sec: 0.2 -> 46.7
cache.entries: 148k -> 12.7k
pool.avg_latency_ms: 38 -> 152 (p50)
p99_latency_ms: 210 -> 980
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Config change applied to hosted-nyc-pool-3 at 12:21 UTC by rashid: runtime.prefix_cache_max_entries=150000 -> 15000 :information_source:

rashid: That change was an intentional memory test for the pool. I did a quick rollout of smaller prefix_cache size to validate memory savings. Didn't expect that level of churn.

alex: Okay that explains the mass evictions. When the cache got trimmed, hit-rate tanked and we started reloading large KV entries a lot. We need to check if any single tenant is creating oversized entries (cache poisoning).

maya: Running a quick query on logs for top prefix sizes...

```
# top offenders by avg_kv_entry_size
tenant: tenant-alpha, avg_entry_size: 1.6MB, 99p_entry_size: 8.3MB, requests: 14k
tenant: tenant-beta, avg_entry_size: 4.1MB, 99p: 18MB, requests: 300
```

alex: Tenant-alpha is our noisy neighbor. They recently started a batch migration that sends very long prefixes (many chat history imports). Those entries blow past our intended size limits and dominate the limited cache after the trim.

rashid: I see — my change set the global entry cap implicitly lower because of overall max entries limit. Combined with a few huge entries, eviction policy started thrashing the cache. We should have a per-entry size cap.

sre-oncall: I've toggled increased alerting and created INC-2025-0823: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-2025-0823 :rotating_light:

alex: Profiling note: when hit-rate collapsed we saw the runtime fall back to generic attention kernels frequently (kernel selection path decided fast_fused_attention was incompatible because KV cache lookups were missing / partial). That fallback increases token decode time substantially.

maya: Relevant profile snippet:

```
[12:23:10] request_id=abcd1234: seq_len=512, kv_cache_miss=true, kernel_chosen=generic_attention, decode_time_ms=1.9/token
[12:23:12] request_id=efgh5678: seq_len=2048, kv_cache_miss=true, kernel_chosen=generic_attention, decode_time_ms=2.6/token
```

alex: Also saw batching heuristics get worse — continuous batching aggregated more requests waiting for KV priming, raising tail latency. The cost of missing KV entries cascades into both kernel selection and batching effects.

rashid: Immediate mitigation options:
- rollback prefix_cache_max_entries to 150k (undo my change)
- apply per-entry size cap (ignore/evict entries > 1MB)
- add fast path: skip storing entries above threshold so they don't pollute cache

maya: Can we evict the biggest offenders now? I can run a targeted evict for tenant-alpha.

alex: Yes, do evict-by-size first then rollback. Evict command (internal API):

```sh
curl -X POST 'https://internal-console/pools/hosted-nyc/prefix_cache/evict' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"criteria":"tenant==\'tenant-alpha\' OR size_bytes>1048576"}'
```

maya: Running eviction now... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: Evict API returned: {"evicted_entries": 412, "freed_bytes": 1.7e9} :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: runtime-metrics: kv_cache.hit_rate -> 64% (12:28 UTC)

alex: Great, hit-rate improving. Let's still revert the config and push a short-term guard in the runtime to reject/stub very large prefix caching.

rashid: Rolling back to 150k now. Pushing change: runtime.config.prefix_cache_max_entries=150000 (rolling restart small subset).

sre-oncall: Noted. Monitoring dashboards updated, setting 1h watch and page on p99>600ms.

maya: After rollback + eviction we see p50~45ms, p99~220ms. Not fully back to baseline but trending.

alex: Postmortem action items (quick):
- Add per-entry size limit (1MB) and ignore-on-store for >limit (owner: eng-runtime/rashid)
- Make eviction policy LRU by weighted size not count (owner: eng-runtime/alex)
- Add alert for sudden global eviction spikes and rate-limit config rollouts (owner: eng-sre)
- Follow-up postmortem doc (owner: maya)

rashid: I'll open the PR for size-limit today and include a canary. Also adding a safety flag so small rollout doesn't OOM a pool by trimming too aggressively.

maya: Thanks all. Filing a short RCA doc and scheduling a follow-up sync in 2 hours. :memo:

sre-oncall: Incident closed to monitoring state, will escalate if regressions in next 60m. :lock:

alex: TL;DR — config change reduced cached entry count, noisy tenant's huge entries dominated the new smaller cache, causing evictions -> hit-rate collapse -> kernel fallback & batching degradation -> latency spike. Fix: evict offenders, rollback, add size caps + weighted eviction.
